title: LUCIE: A Universal Chiplet-Interposer Design Framework for Plug-and-Play Integration
problem: Multi-chip module designs lack a standardized framework for seamless chiplet communication and integration, forcing designers to use custom interposers or NoC-based approaches that are costly, complex, and inflexible.
motivation: Chiplets are a promising approach for post-Moore's Law silicon with benefits like improved yield and heterogeneous integration, but adoption requires standardization and simplified integration.
method: LUCIE provides a standardized middle layer (an interposer) that sits between separate computer chips and handles their communication directly, rather than requiring custom designs. The interposer arranges chips in a 2D grid pattern (like a checkerboard) where each chip connects to its neighbors. A placement algorithm (using graph theory—a mathematical way of mapping connections) automatically figures out where each chip should sit for efficient communication. The framework supports different connection patterns, like grids (2D mesh) or hub-and-spoke arrangements (star topology), all without requiring new engineering for each design.
key_novelty: LUCIE is a reusable grid-based interposer system with automatic chip placement that lets you connect different chips together without designing each connection by hand.
contributions: LUCIE framework: universal, modular, reconfigurable chiplet integration ecosystem
2D grid-based interposer design supporting multiple topologies
Graph-based placement algorithm reducing design complexity
18.9% manufacturing cost savings and 30 weeks time-to-market reduction vs custom interposers

metrics.speedup: 2x faster than NoC-on-NoP in certain scenarios
